ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a 10 V voltage source, with the upper terminal positive and the lower terminal negative. The upper terminal of the voltage source is connected through a 20 kΩ resistor to the upper node on the right. From this upper node, a 20 kΩ resistor is connected downward to the lower common node, and on the right side there is also a 4 µF capacitor connected from the same upper node to the lower common node. The capacitor voltage v_C is labeled as positive at the top and negative at the bottom, and the arrow of the capacitor current i_C points along the upper wire toward the capacitor on the right. Reasoning: According to the specified method, first find the Thevenin equivalent seen from the capacitor port. When the capacitor is open-circuited, the two 20 kΩ resistors form a voltage divider connected across the 10 V source, so the open-circuit voltage of the capacitor upper node is V_th = 10 V × 20 kΩ/(20 kΩ + 20 kΩ) = 5 V. After short-circuiting the 10 V source, looking into the capacitor port, both 20 kΩ resistors are connected to the reference node, so they are in parallel, R_th = 20 kΩ || 20 kΩ = 10 kΩ. The time constant τ = R_th C = 10 kΩ × 4 µF = 0.04 s, so 1/τ = 25 s^-1. Given v_C(0)=0 V, the capacitor charges toward the final value 5 V; according to the positive direction of i_C pointing toward the capacitor in the figure, the initial current is V_th/R_th = 5 V/10 kΩ = 0.50 mA, and it decays exponentially. Therefore i_C(t)=0.50 exp(-25t) mA.

method.method_draft: Compute the Thevenin equivalent seen by the capacitor. With the capacitor open, the two 20 kΩ resistors form a divider across 10 V, so V_th = 5 V. With the 10 V source shorted, the two 20 kΩ resistors are in parallel as seen from the capacitor node, so R_th = 10 kΩ. Then tau = R_th C = 10 kΩ · 4 µF = 0.04 s, so 1/tau = 25 s^-1. Since V_C(0)=0, the initial charging current is V_th/R_th = 5 V/10 kΩ = 0.50 mA, decaying exponentially: i_C(t)=0.50 exp(-25t) mA.

method.method_draft: Let v(t)=v_C(t) be the top-node voltage. KCL at the node gives current entering from the source resistor equal to currents leaving through the shunt resistor and capacitor: (10-v)/20 kΩ = v/20 kΩ + C dv/dt. With C=4 µF, rearrange to dv/dt + 25v = 125, and use v(0)=0. The solution is v(t)=5(1-exp(-25t)) V. Then i_C(t)=C dv/dt = 4 µF · 125 exp(-25t) = 0.50 exp(-25t) mA, in the indicated direction.
